key_insight: Spin-sector dissipation couples spin and orbital angular momentum and drives spin polarization toward thermal vorticity in the simulated expanding fluids.
engineering_relevance: For simulations of spin-polarized fluids, Israel–Stewart dynamics offers a more consistent framework for coupling linear- and angular-momentum conservation than Navier–Stokes dynamics alone.
method: Extend perfect spin hydrodynamics with dissipative, antisymmetric energy–momentum contributions.
Compare Navier–Stokes and Israel–Stewart descriptions of spin relaxation.
Simulate Bjorken expansion and boost-invariant, cylindrically symmetric expansion.
evidence_signal: Numerical results across varied spin kinetic coefficients and relaxation times show polarization approaching thermal vorticity, with Israel–Stewart evolution first approaching the Navier–Stokes regime.
watch_item: Spin kinetic coefficients and relaxation times remain unspecified a priori, while the Navier–Stokes formulation can introduce higher-order derivatives that disrupt the equation structure.
paper_title: Novel hydrodynamic features in dissipative spin-polarized fluids
